chunks.title: Rhetorical Analysis exemplar — Sample 2A, score 1-4-0 (5/6)
chunks.content: Rhetorical Analysis (Gilliland, on reconnecting with nature) scored 5/6 (Thesis 1, Evidence & Commentary 4, Sophistication 0). Thesis (1): defensible thesis naming the rhetorical choices — appeals to family and 'almost outrageous suggestions' — used to emphasize reconnecting with nature. Evidence & Commentary (4): specific evidence for all claims (references to grandmother/mother; 'walk barefoot on the earth'); commentary consistently explains how the evidence supports the reasoning AND how multiple rhetorical choices contribute to the argument. Sophistication (0): situates the argument in a 'post Covid-19 world' but does not show complex understanding of the rhetorical situation.

chunks.subject: AP English Language
chunks.title: Rhetorical Analysis exemplar — Sample 2B, score 1-3-0 (4/6)
chunks.content: Rhetorical Analysis scored 4/6 (Thesis 1, Evidence & Commentary 3, Sophistication 0). Thesis (1): defensible thesis (extended personification of nature and vivid exemplification move readers to go outside). Evidence & Commentary (3): specific evidence for all claims ('My land wanted nothing but flowers'); commentary explains how some evidence supports the reasoning and how at least one rhetorical choice (personification) contributes — but some commentary (about the 'lists') does not clearly connect to the claim, so short of 4. Sophistication (0): recognizes a writer/reader difference but does not explore the article's complexities or tensions.

chunks.subject: AP English Language
chunks.title: Rhetorical Analysis exemplar — Sample 2C, score 1-2-0 (3/6)
chunks.content: Rhetorical Analysis scored 3/6 (Thesis 1, Evidence & Commentary 2, Sophistication 0). Thesis (1): defensible thesis (metaphor and tone highlight the value of engaging with nature). Evidence & Commentary (2): relevant evidence, some specific (barefoot / basil quotes) mixed with broad generalities; commentary explains how some evidence relates to the argument but does not connect it to the claim, so no clear line of reasoning; includes simplistic explanations. Sophistication (0): mentions her role as a writer but does not explore it as part of the rhetorical situation.
